clue.text: More sporting provisions in report on rider's backers

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it
in report means the word is as heard spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: provisions are food supplies, fare

indicators.note: the backers of the rider are its rear letters, the last two of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist's sponsors are said to be offering something more sportsmanlike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in report' makes FARE heard as FAIR; 'backers' takes the back pair of letters, ER, from 'rider'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fair is playing by the rules, so fairer is more sporting in the sense of more sportsmanlike.

clue.text: These French, on a roll, find no place to swim

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: ces is French for these
a spool is a reel or roll of thread or film

explanation.surface: French swimmers on a roll still cannot find a pool to train in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit of sewage is the last place anyone would choose for a dip, an ironic description.

clue.text: Spaced-out Boatman lost bearings around Paris

indicators.note: around says the two compass letters surround the shortened city

parts.note: S and E are compass bearings, south and east

indicators.note: lost says that letter has gone missing from the city name

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter got lost somewhere around Paris and has gone a bit spacey.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I, the first person; 'lost' removes it from Paris to leave PARS, and 'around' puts S and E outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse things are thinly scattered with gaps between, so widely spaced out.

clue.text: Contador, top undone, working up a storm

indicators.note: working up says the remaining letters are stirred into a new arrangement
in a down clue the top is the first letter, and undone says it is taken off

parts.note: Alberto Contador, the Spanish cyclist

explanation.surface: Cyclist Alberto Contador, losing his top jersey, rides furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top undone' takes C off Contador to leave ONTADOR, and 'working up' rearranges it. The surface borrows the idiom 'work up a storm'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm, a kind of storm.

clue.text: Where riders in fleet race round all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cycling fleet races round the country in a sprawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tour de France is the great annual cycle race, the place where professional cyclists compete.

clue.text: Boatman (Boatman?!) said to be a descender?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: said to be means the words are heard when spoken rather than read as written

parts.note: a sailor is a boatman; spoken aloud SAILOR is heard as the end of the answer

explanation.surface: The setter, punning on his own pen name, wonders whether he is a climber coming down a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: AB SAILOR spoken sounds like the answer; the setter's own name, Boatman, is repeated to give both parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An abseiler goes down a rope on a rock face, so a descender, with a question mark for the playful sense.

clue.text: Redress nature of regressive Right

parts.note: one's make-up is one's nature or character

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the little word before it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A reactionary right wing is in its very nature something to fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' looks like a political jibe at the Right, but it only turns the little word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to compensate for it, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Race shows guts of rider, Byelorussian

indicators.note: shows the guts of means the inner part of these words displays the letters, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A Belarusian rider shows courage in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is a famous English horse race run at Epsom, and the word is used for races generally.

clue.text: Rider penalised, prepares for a fight: conduct ultimately improper, they say

parts.note: to arm is to prepare for battle, so arms means prepares for a fight

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows
they say signals that the word is heard rather than spelt, dropping its silent first letter

parts.note: improper conduct is wrong

explanation.surface: A cyclist is punished after squaring up for a fight, behaviour judged improper.
explanation.walkthrough: WRONG spoken sounds like RONG, which is the spelling used here. Lance Armstrong was stripped of his Tour de France titles for doping.
explanation.definitionFit: Lance Armstrong, the American cyclist, was banned and lost his titles: a rider who was penalised.

clue.text: Personal opinion expressed here on podium finish by bike

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another follows it
the finish of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an op-ed is the newspaper page where columnists give personal opinions

explanation.surface: A rider's personal view, given after reaching the podium on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motorbike with pedals, a kind of bike.

clue.text: Go quickly on descent: evidence of regret?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: to tear along is to go very fast
a drop is a fall or descent

explanation.surface: A cyclist speeding downhill fears a crash he may come to rue.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling tear on the cheek shows sorrow or remorse, hence regret, with a question mark for the example.

clue.text: Rider, a man of iron, grabs opportunity

indicators.note: grabs says the symbol holds the other word inside it

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
room is scope or opportunity, as in room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A tough cyclist seizes his chance to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Froome won the Tour de France in 2016 and was leading it when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Froome is a British cyclist, a male Tour de France rider.

clue.text: Depressingly, rider lay injured

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so these letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Sadly, a cyclist lies hurt after a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearily means in a dull, gloomy way, a near synonym of depressingly.

clue.text: Anticipating feverish duel, Europe embraces the crossbar!

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so this part leads
embraces says the European letters hold the cross between them

parts.note: EC, the European Community
X is a cross

indicators.note: feverish means agitated, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Before a heated duel, Europe hugs the crossbar, as if at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossbar' must be split: 'cross' is X and 'bar' is the definition; 'feverish' rearranges the duel.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to shut them out or keep them away, a synonym.

clue.text: Copying style? Ignore two times

indicators.note: style, as a verb, means fashion or shape, so the letters are fashioned anew

parts.note: X is the times sign, so two of them give XX

explanation.surface: A style of imitation that pays no attention to the multiplication table.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerox is a photocopier brand name, used as a verb for making photocopies.

clue.text: See 11
Wheeler-dealers substituting one of riders after start of Tour

indicators.note: after says the changed word follows that opening letter
start of points to the first letter of the word
one can be I or A, so one 'one' replaces the other in the word

explanation.surface: Wheeling and dealing as one rider is swapped for another early in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: Both I and A can mean one; swapping the I in RIDERS for A gives RADERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Traders buy and sell, the trade of wheeler-dealers, though with less shady flavour.

clue.text: See 5
Rider triumphs, taking on Italian legend with force

indicators.note: taking on means admitting or containing, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: wins means triumphs
leg end: the end of the word leg is G
g stands for the force of gravity in physics

explanation.surface: A champion cyclist wins, taking on an Italian great with power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' is read as 'leg end', the last letter of LEG. Bradley Wiggins won the Tour de France in 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bradley Wiggins is a British cyclist, a Tour de France and Olympic rider.

clue.text: Brassica, some brown cabbage and cauliflower heads and cooking oil

indicators.note: some of means just part of the word, its opening letters, with the tail dropped
heads are the first letters of each word
cooking means being prepared, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe list: brassicas, brown cabbage, cauliflower and oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes BRO from brown; 'heads' takes C and C; 'cooking' rearranges OIL to OLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family, the brassicas.

clue.text: Perhaps rider in lead to take on large entry

indicators.note: take on means admit or include, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to cause is to lead to a result

explanation.surface: A cyclist in front taking on a big entry.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider in law is an added clause in a document; 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a contract or bill, so a rider is one example of a clause.

clue.text: Reply exposing fallacy, using tenets extant ab initio

definitions.text: Reply exposing fallacy, using tenets extant ab initio

indicators.note: ab initio is Latin for from the beginning, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebuttal attacks a fallacy using established principles from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute is to disprove, a reply that exposes an argument as false.

clue.text: King of the Mountains' features: most fans need them

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
o' is a shortened of, as in o'clock
tors are rocky peaks, features of mountains

explanation.surface: The polka-dot jersey winner's fans need the hills he conquers.
explanation.walkthrough: King of the Mountains is the title for the Tour's best climber, but here it splits into R, O and TORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric fans spin blades on a rotating part, so most fans need rotors.

clue.text: Where more than one rider is seen in A & E

definitions.text: Where more than one rider is seen

indicators.note: in says the letters wanted lie inside the full name, spanning its words, with the rest discarded

parts.note: A & E is the British hospital emergency department, Accident and Emergency

explanation.surface: Several riders end up in hospital after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out A & E as accident and emergency, the British hospital casualty department; the letters are found across its words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem bicycle seats two or more riders one behind another.

clue.text: An Englishman in France, perhaps unknown during record comeback

indicators.note: during means within, so the letter goes inside
comeback means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tape is a recording
x is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An English exile in France makes a comeback on record.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat lives abroad, and a Briton living in France is one example.

clue.text: They race across France, starving, beaten on top of the Tourmalet

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another follows it
the top of a word is its first letter
beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Starving riders are beaten at the summit of the Tourmalet climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The Col du Tourmalet is a famous Pyrenean climb in the Tour. TGVs are France's high-speed trains.
explanation.definitionFit: TGV trains run at high speed across French territory, so they race across France.

clue.text: No! Time flies before hard grind

indicators.note: before says the shortened insects come ahead
No here means without, taking that letter away from the insects

parts.note: gnats are small flies
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Time flies, as the saying goes, before the hard slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes T out of GNATS to leave GNAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash or grind your teeth is the same action, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: He was close to a beast and, in a way, closer

definitions.text: He was close to a beast

indicators.note: in a way here means in some different manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who was near an animal and, in some sense, nearer still.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw and was later spared by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcles, of the Roman tale, befriended a lion, so he was close to a wild animal.
